answer: Bone turning keeps Sybils out. A newcomer turns 24 buttons across 22 days while two button-makers from separate workshops measure each button's diameter to within 1 millimeter, logging every one on the button board beside a plume mark. Miss by more than 2 millimeters and that button loses its credit, turning pauses 14 days; three bad buttons void the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents means 24,000 buttons and 48,000 checks, roughly $150,000 in wages, while one honest agent just keeps turning. Like a grove where only trees fed on real nectar bear fruit, only work truly done earns standing.
